question: For the three New Mexico expungement families this lane claimed, what does each bound official document actually contain — measured first hand from the pinned binaries — and what would a builder have to declare?
whyThisFileExists: The three New Mexico families were claimed, their sources were resolved by content hash and every byte is held, and they were then returned unbuilt on a completeness-contract question rather than a source one. These measurements are the part of the work that is finished and transferable: every blank on every bound document, read from the pinned bytes, so the lane that builds these families starts from a measured census rather than from the page.
whatThisIsNot: a field map, a build, a verdict, or an authority to write anything. Nothing here classifies a blank.
measuredFrom: the Master Library mount, resolved by SHA-256 across every custody the committed corpus index names

howBlanksWereMeasured.underscore_run: contiguous U+005F glyphs on one baseline, from the per-glyph x and advance the shared anchor-capture walker reports; runs abutting across two text-showing operators are joined at a 1.2pt tolerance and a run of fewer than three glyphs is not a blank
howBlanksWereMeasured.stroke: a filled horizontal rectangle of width >= 12pt read from the page content stream by the shared rule-line reader; never from a raster
howBlanksWereMeasured.bracket_box: a printed "[ ]" selection control, located from the per-glyph positions of the bracket pair
howBlanksWereMeasured.howAnUnderlineIsToldFromABlank: a stroke carrying printed glyphs on it, at a baseline within 13pt above it and overlapping its own x span, is an underline of printed text and not a blank. New Mexico rule forms use underlining and bracketing to mark amended text, so a builder that read every stroke as a blank would invent write boxes under the amendment marks.
